Listing Alert MIAX Sapphire October 01, 2026 | 01:57 PM MIAX Exchange Group - Options Markets - Corporate Action Alert: UWM Holdings Corporation (UWMC) (UWMC1) UWM Holdings Corporation (UWMC) has declared a rights distribution effective for Friday, October 2, 2026. UWMC should be used for class assignments in UWMC1 via MFP All LMM and RMM Option Class Assignments must be entered prior to 6:00 PM ET on the business day immediately preceding the effective date. All changes made after 6:00 PM ET on a given day will be effective two trading days later. Additional details about the UWM Holdings Corporation (UWMC) rights distribution are provided in the attached OCC Memo. Please contact MIAX Listings with any questions at Listings@miaxglobal.com or (609) 897-7308. UWMC Distribution 59834

title: MIAX Exchange Group - Options Markets - Qualified Securities for Q4 2026
raw_text:
MIAX Sapphire — Listing Alert — MIAX Exchange Group - Options Markets - Qualified Securities for Q4 2026
Listing Alert MIAX Sapphire October 01, 2026 | 05:57 PM MIAX Exchange Group - Options Markets - Qualified Securities for Q4 2026 As previously announced in the January 20, 2026 Alert and August 17, 2026 Alert, the MIAX Options Exchanges filed with the SEC to amend the Short Term Option Series Program of each exchange. The Short Term Option Series Program was amended to include, in addition to the up to two Monday and Wednesday expirations for options on certain individual stocks: (1) adding up to two Tuesday and Thursday expirations for options on Exchange-Traded Fund ("ETF") Shares that meet a higher threshold of criteria "Qualifying Securities" criteria, and (2) adding up to two Monday and Wednesday expirations for options on ETF Shares that meet a lower-threshold set of criteria. A Qualifying Security is (1) an underlying security, as measured on the last day of the prior calendar quarter, must have: (A) a market capitalization of greater than 700 billion dollars for an individual stock based on the closing price, or (B) (i) Assets under Management (“AUM”) greater than 50 billion dollars for an Exchange-Traded Fund Share based on net asset value (“NAV”); or (ii) AUM greater than 25 billion dollars for an Exchange-Traded Fund Share based on NAV; (2) monthly options volume, as measured by sides traded in the last month preceding the quarter end, of greater than 10 million options; or monthly options volume, as measured by sides traded in the last month preceding the quarter end, of greater than 5 million options for an Exchange-Traded Fund Share that qualified for (B)(ii) above; (3) a position limit of at least 250,000 contracts; and (4) participate in the Penny Interval Program. ETFs meeting the criteria of an AUM greater than $50 billion, monthly options volume greater than 10 million contracts, a position limit of at least 250,000 contracts, and participation in the Penny Interval Program, are "Tier 1 Qualifying Securities" and are eligible for up to two Monday/Tuesday/ Wednesday/ Thursday expirations. ETFs meeting the criteria of an AUM greater than $25 billion, monthly options volume greater than 5 million contracts, a position limit of at least 250,000 contracts, and participation in the Penny Interval Program, are "Tier 2 Qualifying Securities" and are eligible for up to two Monday and Wednesday expirations. The new series will follow the existing Short Term Option Series Program process of same strike-price intervals, P.M.-settled, and skips any week where the expiration would coincide with a standard, monthly, or quarterly expiration. A Qualifying Security expiration would not be listed on a day when there will be an earnings announcement that takes place after market close. The following securities are Qualified Securities for Q4 2026: Individual Stock Qualifying Securities: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) Alphabet, Inc. (GOOGL) Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) Apple Inc. (AAPL) Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) Meta Platforms, Inc. (META) Micron Technology, Inc. (MU) Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) ETF Tier 1 Qualifying Securities: Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF) iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) ETF Tier 2 Qualifying Securities: iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF (IEF) iShares iBoxx $ Invst Grade Corporate Bond ETF (LQD) iShares Silver Trust (SLV) iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF (GDX) ProShares UltraPro QQQ (TQQQ) Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE) VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) Each calendar quarter, the above criteria will be reassessed to determine eligibility for the following quarter as a Qualifying Security. The MIAX Option Exchanges will post the list of Qualifying Securities on our website by the close of business on the first trading day of each quarter. Please contact MIAX Listings with any questions at Listings@miaxglobal.com or (609) 897-7308.

A Qualifying Security is (1) an underlying security, as measured on the last day of the prior calendar quarter, must have: (A) a market capitalization of greater than 700 billion dollars for an individual stock based on the closing price, or (B) (i) Assets under Management (“AUM”) greater than 50 billion dollars for an Exchange-Traded Fund Share based on net asset value (“NAV”); or (ii) AUM greater than 25 billion dollars for an Exchange-Traded Fund Share based on NAV; (2) monthly options volume, as measured by sides traded in the last month preceding the quarter end, of greater than 10 million options; or monthly options volume, as measured by sides traded in the last month preceding the quarter end, of greater than 5 million options for an Exchange-Traded Fund Share that qualified for (B)(ii) above; (3) a position limit of at least 250,000 contracts; and (4) participate in the Penny Interval Program. ETFs meeting the criteria of an AUM greater than $50 billion, monthly options volume greater than 10 million contracts, a position limit of at least 250,000 contracts, and participation in the Penny Interval Program, are "Tier 1 Qualifying Securities" and are eligible for up to two Monday/Tuesday/ Wednesday/ Thursday expirations. ETFs meeting the criteria of an AUM greater than $25 billion, monthly options volume greater than 5 million contracts, a position limit of at least 250,000 contracts, and participation in the Penny Interval Program, are "Tier 2 Qualifying Securities" and are eligible for up to two Monday and Wednesday expirations. The new series will follow the existing Short Term Option Series Program process of same strike-price intervals, P.M.-settled, and skips any week where the expiration would coincide with a standard, monthly, or quarterly expiration. title: Investment Company Cross Trading
raw_text:
Investment Company Cross Trading

The Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission") is proposing to amend the rule under the Investment Company Act of 1940 (the "Investment Company Act") that permits securities transactions between a registered investment company and certain affiliates (referred to as "cross trades"), subject to conditions. The proposed amendments are designed to expand the scope of securities that are eligible for cross trading, modernize the rule's conditions, and enhance investor protection. The Commission also proposes to require aggregated reporting of trading activity and cross trades in Form N- PORT and Form N-MFP.

title: Adviser and Regulated Fund Custody Rules; Crypto Custody Rules
raw_text:
Adviser and Regulated Fund Custody Rules; Crypto Custody Rules

The Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission" or the "SEC") is proposing new custody rules under the Investment Company Act of 1940 (the "Investment Company Act") and amendments to related reporting and recordkeeping requirements to address how regulated investment companies may custody crypto securities and similar investments, and amendments to the custody rule and related reporting and recordkeeping rules under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the "Advisers Act") to address how registered investment advisers may custody client crypto funds and securities. We are also proposing to amend the current custody rules to modernize their requirements, to better address current industry practices and feedback, and to implement certain conforming amendments. We are also proposing amendments to the recordkeeping rules under the Investment Company Act and Advisers Act related to these proposed modernization amendments to the custody rules. Additionally, we are proposing to redesignate the custody rule under the Advisers Act and to make corresponding amendments to Form ADV and Form ADV-E for registered investment advisers to reflect the Advisers Act custody rule redesignation. We are also proposing amendments to Form ADV for registered investment advisers and Form N-CEN for regulated investment companies and to improve the quality of public disclosures made on these forms. We are also proposing to add new questions to Form ADV and Form N-CEN related to tokenized private funds and regulated investment company shares, respectively.

title: D33. How should the tradingSession field be populated for option orders?
raw_text:
D33. How should the tradingSession field be populated for option orders?

The tradingSession must be populated with the trading session(s) during which an order is eligible to trade.

For certain options that are eligible to trade on the Cboe Exchange, Inc. during extended global market hours sessions (generally from 8:15 pm T-1 to 9:15 am Eastern Time) and/or regular market hours sessions, the tradingSession field must be populated with:

-    'REG' (Regular Only), for orders only eligible to trade during regular market hours; or 
-    'ALL' (All Sessions), for orders eligible to trade during extended global market hours, regular market hours, and the Curb session.
-    'REGPOST' (Regular and Post Market), for orders eligible to trade during regular market hours and the Curb session.

Technical Alert, Trading Alert MIAX Pearl Equities October 13, 2026 | 08:50 AM MIAX Pearl Equities Exchange - Reminder: 2026 Technology Refresh of Matching Engine, FOI, FIX Drop, MEO and Market Data Retransmission Servers in NY4 - October 17 Test As previously announced in the September 17, 2026 and September 28, 2026 Alerts, MIAX Pearl Equities Exchange will complete a technology upgrade of the trading platform servers in NY4 to enhance system performance. This upgrade requires no changes by member firms. Member firms' connectivity, functionality and interfaces will not be impacted or require any updates. The technology upgrade will be completed in phases. For each phase, the cut-over work supporting the technology refresh for the client facing apps will be performed after trading on Friday evenings beginning at 8:30 p.m. ET and connectivity testing will be available the following Saturday for each phase as outlined below. Technology upgrade phases: Phase Two – October 2026 and November 2026 - Primary hosts for the Matching Engines, Market Data feeds and Retransmission systems, FIX gateways and MEO gateways Phase Three – Late November 2026 and early December 2026 - Secondary hosts for Matching Engine, Market Data feeds, FIX and MEO gateways Connectivity testing prior to production activation will be available on the following dates. title: MIAX Pearl Equities - Post Mortem for Abnormal Latency in Publication Path to the UTP SIP

MIAX Pearl Equities — Regulatory Alert, Technical Alert, Trading Alert — MIAX Pearl Equities - Post Mortem for Abnormal Latency in Publication Path to the UTP SIP
Regulatory Alert, Technical Alert, Trading Alert MIAX Pearl Equities October 12, 2026 | 02:47 PM MIAX Pearl Equities - Post Mortem for Abnormal Latency in Publication Path to the UTP SIP As previously announced in the 9:28 a.m. Alert , MIAX Pearl Equities investigated and resolved abnormal latency in the publication path to the UTP SIP between 4:00 a.m. and 9:03 a.m. ET. A UTP SIP software maintenance job was completed after MIAX Pearl Equities connected which forced a disconnect. After unsuccessfully trying to reestablish connectivity to the UTP SIP LDC (Local Data Center), MIAX connected to the RDC (Remote Data Center). At 9:03 a.m. ET, MIAX forced connectivity back to the UTP SIP LDC. There was no misconfiguration on MIAX Pearl Equities. Market Data was published to both UTP SIP and direct market feeds without delay. MIAX Pearl Equities has taken further steps to monitor UTP SIP connectivity to ensure we are connected to the optimal path. If you have any questions, please contact MIAX Trading Operations at TradingOperations@miaxglobal.com or (609) 897-7302. Regulatory inquiries should be directed to Regulatory@miaxglobal.com or (609) 897-7309.

The new products will go live on the MIAX Futures Onyx Commodities Trading Platform in the CH4 Data Center. Market participants should ensure clearing arrangements are in place with MIAX Futures Clearing Members, as the new futures products will clear through the MIAX Futures Clearing House. New Products: Urea - Product Group Code ‘MGU' Mono-Ammonium Phosphate - Product Group Code ‘MAP’ Di-Ammonium Phosphate - Product Group Code ‘DAP’ Potassium Chloride - Product Group Code ‘MOP’ Important Details: New products are available in the Firm Test Bed. Market data dissemination for the new Fertilizer Futures Products including Cross Product Spreads began on the evening of Sunday, October 4, 2026 for the Monday, October 5, 2026 trade date. Testing Opportunity: New OPRA Dynamic Rebalance Symbol Distribution - Industry Test #3 - Saturday, October 17, 2026 - Reminder
1 October 9, 2026 To: OPRA Multicast Subscribers Subject: Testing Opportunity: New OPRA Dynamic Rebalance Symbol Distribution - Industry Test #3 - Saturday, October 17, 2026 - Reminder What’s New: As previously announced, OPRA is implementing a change to its current message traffic distribution and balancing methodology, effective November 23, 2026. To support industry readiness efforts, the OPRA SIP will conduct its third industry test on Saturday, October 17, 2026, providing subscribers and downstream consumers an opportunity to validate their environment and preparedness ahead of the production rollout. Certification (Cert) System Testing • Available as of Monday, August 24, 2026 (Functional testing) Planned Industry Test dates • Saturday, August 29, 2026 (Functional testing) - Completed • Saturday, October 3, 2026 (Functional, Failure/Recovery, and Capacity testing) - Completed • Saturday, October 17, 2026 (Intraday fallback to November 20, 2026, symbol routing) • Saturday, October 31, 2026 (Final Functional testing) • Saturday, November 21, 2026 (Confidence Test prior to Go-Live) • Monday, November 23, 2026: Activation Go-Live Test Plan and Participation Registration • The test plan and schedule can be found on the next page of this notice. • To participate, your firm must register by completing and submitting the Participation Form. Data Subscribers who receive OPRA from connectivity service providers other than ICE Global Network (IGN) or the NMS Network must contact their connectivity service providers to coordinate testing. Documentation Following documents have been updated. • OPRA Pillar Output Specification • Common IP Multicast Distribution Network Specification • Multicast Channel Dynamic Balancing Plan Technical Inquiries • NMS Product Management Support Email: CTA-OPRA-Support@siac.com • NMS Product Management Support Line: 212-656-8177, Option 2 • NMS Product Management Phone Support Hours: 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM ET Securities Industry Automation Corporation 11 Wall Street, New York, NY 10005 Securities Industry Automation Corporation 11 Wall Street, New York, NY 10005 2 # Time Test Category Action By Test Description Expected Results Friday, October 16 1 11:30:00 PM Series Mapping File OPRA OPRA to generate Series Mapping File (OPRASymbolMapping_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.csv) File available at https://ftp.nyse.com/opra_symbol_files, containing mapping of series to the output lines effective for Saturday Saturday, October 17 2 2:10:00 - 2:30 AM* SOD OPRA OPRA to trigger Start of Day message 3 2:10:00 - 2:45 AM* Series Mapping Messages OPRA OPRA to publish real-time Series Mapping (Category R Type A) Messages providing Series to Output Line mapping (same mapping as available in the Series Mapping File) Series Mapping Messages published on the respective multicast output line to which the series is assigned for the day. In addition, messages also published over the output dedicated multicast output line #220 Participants Participants to establish connectivity for OPRA Input lines on Primary Data Center Participants establish connections Participants Participants to start submitting Quote and Trade data Quotes and trades accepted and disseminated via the multicast output lines in Primary Data Center, as per the provided series distribution 5 9:30:00 AM Market Open OPRA Market Open 6 9:30:00 AM - 10:15:00 AM Data Verification Participants Participants to continue submitting Quote and Trade data -- Data Subscribers can verify Data over the multicast output lines as per the provided series distribution -- Data Subscribers can request retransmission as needed. Retransmitted data will be distributed according to the provided series distribution OPRA to initiate fallback to the alpha-range symbol distribution, which involves software rollback and system cold restart in the Primary Data Center (LDC). -- Disconnection of all OPRA Input and Retransmission lines for all Participants and Data Subscribers -- Disruption in output multicast data dissemination for all lines Upon Fallback completion, OPRA to publish following messages on the LDC output lines: 1) Reset Block Sequence Number (Category H Type K) for each OPRA output line to reset the sequence number to 1 2) Zero Quotes (Quote messages with Zero Price and Size) on behalf of all participants across all symbols Note: 1) Messages will be published based on the alpha-range symbol distribution that is currently effective in Production (refer 'OPRA Symbol Distribution Table' under https://www.opraplan.com/document-library for current symbol distribution) 2) Series Mapping (Category R Type A) message or a series mapping file will not be available -- Data Subscribers to make any necessary changes at their end to handle updated symbol distribution intraday. -- Data Subscribers to receive and process sequence reset and Zero quote messages disseminated from the LDC based on alpha- range symbol distribution (series to output line mapping will be different from prior to fallback) -- Retransmission for any gaps prior to the fallback will not be available. Any new gaps after the fallback (after the sequence reset to 1) can be retransmitted on the LDC. Data Subscriber would be required to apply the offset up to 4,294,967,295 in the message sequence number when sending the retransmission requests. OPRA to enable Input and Retransmission lines on the LDC site LDC Input IP/Ports available to establish connections (connectivity to DR Data Center will not be available) Participants to reconnect to OPRA on their Input IP/Ports on OPRA LDC and establish sequence numbers by sending Block Sequence Number Status Inquiry Request (Category N / Type L) and Message Count Status Inquiry Request (Category N / Type R). OPRA to accept input connections and respond with Block Sequence Response (Category N / Type M) and Message Count Status Response (Category N / Type S), providing the latest sequence numbers, as previously processed over the LDC prior to the fallback Participants to start submitting quote and trade data from the latest Sequence Numbers -- Data Subscribers to accept and process quotes and trades disseminated on the output lines as per the alpha-range symbol distribution 8 10:30:00 AM - 11:30:00 AM Data Verification Participants Participants to continue submitting Quote and Trade data -- Data Subscribers can verify Data over the multicast output lines as per the alpha-range symbol distribution -- Data Subscribers can request retransmission as needed. Retransmitted data will be distributed according to the alpha-range symbol distribution 11:30:00 AM End of test * SOD, Series Mapping Message dissemination, and Participant Connectivity/Input start times are for weekend testing only. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc.; Order Approving a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Partial Amendment No. 1, To Amend FINRA Rule 2210 (Communications With the Public)
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc.; Order Approving a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Partial Amendment No. 1, To Amend FINRA Rule 2210 (Communications With the Public)

I. Introduction On February 10, 2026, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. (``FINRA'') filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (``SEC'' or ``Commission''), pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (``Exchange Act'') and Rule 19b-4 thereunder, a proposed rule change to amend FINRA Rule 2210 (Communications with the Public) to allow a member broker-dealer (``member'') to project performance or provide a targeted return with respect to a security, a securities portfolio, or an asset allocation or other investment strategy in its communications with the public, subject to specified conditions. The proposed rule change was published for public comment in the Federal Register on February 25, 2026. The comment period closed on March 18, 2026. The Commission received comment letters in response to the Notice. On April 7, 2026, FINRA consented to extend until May 26, 2026, the time period in which the Commission must approve the proposed rule change, disapprove the proposed rule change, or institute proceedings to determine whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule change. On May 18, 2026, the Commission received a letter from FINRA stating, among other things, that it anticipated submitting a response to comments, as well as amendments to the proposed rule change. On May 20, 2026, the Commission published an order instituting proceedings to determine whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule change (``OIP''). The Commission received comment letters in response to the OIP. On June 30, 2026, FINRA responded to the comment letters received in response to the Notice and OIP and filed a partial amendment to the proposed rule change (``Partial Amendment No. 1''). The proposed rule change, as modified by Partial Amendment No. 1 (hereinafter referred to as the ``proposed rule change'' unless otherwise stated), was published for public comment in the Federal Register on July 7, 2026. On July 21, 2026, FINRA consented to extend until October 23, 2026, the time period in which the Commission must approve or disapprove the proposed rule change. The Commission received comment letters in response to Notice II. On October 14, 2026, FINRA responded to the comment letters received in response to Notice II. This order approves the proposed rule change. II. Description of the Proposed Rule Change FINRA Rule 2210 generally prohibits communications with the public that predict or project performance. As discussed below, there are three exceptions to this general prohibition; the proposed rule change would create a fourth exception in limited circumstances. A. FINRA Rule 2210 (Communications With the Public) Among other things, FINRA Rule 2210 imposes restrictions on the content of a member's communications with the public. For example, FINRA Rule 2210(d)(1) (General Standards) (hereinafter the ``general content standards'') requires, among other things, that: (1) all member communications be based on principles of fair dealing and good faith, be fair and balanced, and provide a sound basis for evaluating the facts in regard to any particular security or type of security, industry, or service; and (2) the member: (a) not omit any material fact or qualification if the omission, in light of the context of the material presented, would cause the communication to be misleading; (b) not make any false, exaggerated, unwarranted, promissory, or misleading statement or claim in the communication; and (c) consider the nature of the audience to which the communication will be directed and provide details and explanations appropriate to the audience. The general content standards also prohibit a communication prepared by a member from predicting or projecting performance, implying that past performance will recur, or making any exaggerated or unwarranted claim, opinion, or forecast. This general prohibition, however, does not apply to communications that contain: (1) certain hypothetical illustrations of mathematical principles; (2) certain investment analysis tools or written reports produced by such investment analysis tools; and (3) certain price targets contained in research reports on debt or equity securities. B. The Proposed Rule Change The proposed rule change would adopt a fourth exception to FINRA Rule 2210(d)(1)(F) to permit members' communications to project performance or provide targeted returns with respect to a security, a securities portfolio, or an asset allocation or other investment strategy (hereinafter, ``projected performance or targeted returns''), subject to the conditions described, in turn, below. 1. Written Policies and Procedures The proposed rule change would require any member that communicates projected performance or targeted returns to adopt and implement written policies and procedures reasonably designed to ensure that the communication is relevant to the likely financial situation and investment objectives of the intended audience of the communication. FINRA stated that, under such reasonably designed policies and procedures, a communication containing projected performance or targeted returns should only be distributed to investors whom a member reasonably believes have access to resources to independently analyze this information and who have the financial expertise to understand the risks and limitations of these types of presentations (referred to herein collectively as ``investors who have the resources and financial expertise''). FINRA stated that the proposed rule change generally would not permit the inclusion of projected performance or targeted returns in communications for a mass audience or intended for general circulation, including a general retail investor audience, as in such mass communications, a member generally could not form any expectation that the communication is relevant to the likely financial situation and investment objectives of the intended audience. Trading Alert, Clearing Alert MIAX Futures October 20, 2026 | 02:23 PM MIAX Futures Exchange - Onyx Trading Platform and Clearing System - Reminder: FIA Disaster Recovery Testing on Saturday, October 24, 2026 As previously announced in the September 10, 2026 , September 22, 2026 and October 07, 2026 Alerts, MIAX Futures Exchange will participate in the industry-wide Futures Industry Association (“FIA”) sponsored Disaster Recovery (“DR”) test on Saturday, October 24, 2026. U.S. futures exchanges, clearing houses, futures commission merchants, back-office providers, and data vendors will test connectivity and functionality between DR sites. Although your firm may work with a technology vendor to complete required test components, each Clearing Member is responsible for certification of final test results. October 24, 2026: Test Script Clearing Members must complete the following four test components during the DR test: Trade Entry – MIAX Futures Onyx Trading Platform All Clearing Members must send at least two orders and receive at least one Commodities execution confirmation. Additionally, all Clearing Members with connections to Financial Futures Trading Platform (NY5), must send at least two orders and receive at least one Financial Futures execution confirmation. Products: Hard Red Spring Wheat Futures (MWE) i.e. MWEZ6 Hard Red Spring Wheat Options (OMW) i.e. OMWZ6 C0750 Bloomberg 100 Index (TBQ) i.e. TBQZ26 Bloomberg 500 Index (TBX) i.e. TBXZ26 Prices in MIAX Futures products should be entered at the previous day’s settlement price to ensure your orders match with other participants. October 24, 2026 Test Day Timeline: 7:30 a.m. CT – Firms can connect to the Trading Systems 7:45 a.m. CT – Live Order Window (LOW) First Pre-Opening 8:30 a.m. CT – Opening 12:00 p.m. CT – Closing MIAX Futures will provide updates as to exact pre-open and open times via the FIA conference bridge available. The trade file name will correspond with the new convention being used today, i.e. – TRXzz_yyyymmdd.txt (where zz equates to the Clearing Firm code & yyyymmdd equals trade date). Post Trade Documentation – Submit to MIAX Futures After completing the above steps, Clearing Members must submit the SFTP file available via the MIAX Futures DR SFTP site to MIAX Futures by emailing MIAXFuturesClearingOperations@miaxglobal.com . title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; CME Securities Clearing Inc.; Notice of Filing of Proposed Rule Change To Amend the CMESC Risk Management Framework (“RMF”) Related to CMESC's Default Management Practices
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; CME Securities Clearing Inc.; Notice of Filing of Proposed Rule Change To Amend the CMESC Risk Management Framework (“RMF”) Related to CMESC's Default Management Practices

1. Purpose Background CMESC's default management procedures cover the management of a default of either a Member or User (collectively, ``Participants'') and are designed to ensure the continuity of CMESC's clearance and settlement functions and particularly, the ongoing maintenance of the services provided to non-defaulting Participants, while supporting market integrity and minimizing market disruptions. The primary purpose of the proposed rule change is to enhance the default management process by further codifying the documentation of the default management procedures in the RMF. In particular, the proposed rule change would amend the RMF to (i) provide additional detail around arrangements involving a third-party liquidation agent for managing a Participant default, and (ii) make certain clarifying and administrative changes, where appropriate, in the RMF; and (iii) to clarify the role of CMESC's Risk Management Committee (``CSRMC'') in designing the default management procedures. Liquidation Agent and Execution Brokers Section 14.1.1 (``Participant Default Management Process'') of the RMF would be amended to specify that the close-out process of a defaulted Participant's portfolio may include the use of a liquidation agent and one or more execution brokers. Broadly, the amended RMF would provide that, in managing a default, CMESC and any liquidation agent will collaborate to assess the exposures of the defaulted Participant's portfolio, including associated settlement obligations as they come due, and formulate a close-out strategy under the prevailing market conditions to minimize potential losses and market disruptions and to support market integrity. More specifically, the amended RMF would describe the expectations for a third-party liquidation agent, if used, to assist CMESC with designing and executing the close-out strategy for the defaulted Participant's portfolio. In accordance with the amended RMF, the liquidation agent will be expected to coordinate with CMESC to reconcile positions of the defaulted Participant and assess the outstanding exposure of the defaulted Participant over the course of managing the default. The amended RMF also would provide that the liquidation agent may use various methods to execute close-out trades, including, but not limited to, executing open market transactions; enter into hedging transactions to mitigate the risk of the defaulted Participant's portfolio; and perform other related tasks appropriate to assist CMESC in managing the risk from the Participant's default. In addition, Section 14.1.1 of the RMF would recognize that CMESC may engage one or more execution brokers to coordinate with the liquidation agent and CMESC to provide certain operational services related to the close-out trades arranged or executed by the liquidation agent in managing a default. The amended RMF would include new language to specify that, where appropriate, CMESC would maintain an account with the execution broker where it would be the principal, and the execution broker may submit back-to-back trades that mirror the liquidation agent's close- out trades. CMESC would further specify in the RMF that the submission of back-to-back trades is expected to ensure that CMESC's account at the execution broker maintains a net flat position and facilitate CMESC's ability to meet the settlement obligations of the defaulted Participant as they come due. Clarifying and Administrative Changes The proposed rule change would also include certain clarifying and administrative changes. Member Default: For example, Section 14 (``Default Management'') of the RMF would be amended to clarify that CMESC analyzes Users' risk profile on an ex ante basis. The associated monitoring and analysis serves to improve the likelihood that non-defaulted Users' positions can be transferred to a Member in good standing where their authorizing Member has defaulted. Additionally, the RMF would be amended to clarify that, while CMESC makes its best efforts to transfer non-defaulting Users' positions (i.e., of a defaulted Member) to non-defaulting Members, CMESC continues to monitor Users' positions and the sufficiency of the associated collateral throughout the default management process and based on the prevailing facts and circumstances may close-out (e.g., liquidate) the positions of some or all Users of a defaulted Member. User Default: Section 14.1 (``Participant Default Event'') of the RMF would be updated to specify that an authorizing Member of a defaulted User must respond to CMESC within a period of time prescribed by the Corporation if it wishes to manage the User's default and, if it elects to do so, CMESC will undertake several operational steps relating to the User's positions and collateral to facilitate the Member's management of the User's default in accordance with the CMESC Rules. Section 14.1 of the RMF would also be amended to include ``close-out'' in addition to bidding on or purchasing a defaulted Participant's portfolio when gauging Participants' interest prior to declaring another Participant in default. Additionally, Section 14.1 of the RMF would be amended to clarify that, for Users with multiple authorizing Members, where CMESC manages the User's default, the default management costs will be allocated on a pro rata basis based on the margin requirement for the User's positions authorized by each such Member. Moreover, Section 14.1 would be amended to add that the trades of the Users that are expected to settle on the next day after the day of the Member's default may settle prior to the transfer of any other positions. Participant Default, Generally: The amended RMF also clarifies certain operational steps CMESC would take if it were to manage a default of a Participant itself. Section 14.1.1 of the amended RMF would provide that CMESC will take appropriate operational steps, as soon as practicable, to contain risk and prevent any unauthorized movement of the default Part

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 11.1(a)(3) To Describe When Unpriced Orders Are Eligible for Execution and To Amend Rule 11.6(q)(2) To Clarify the Expiration of Day Orders Entered During the Overnight Trading Session or Order Acceptance Queueing Time
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 11.1(a)(3) To Describe When Unpriced Orders Are Eligible for Execution and To Amend Rule 11.6(q)(2) To Clarify the Expiration of Day Orders Entered During the Overnight Trading Session or Order Acceptance Queueing Time

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 11.1(a)(3) to introduce rule text to describe when orders that do not contain a limit price are eligible for execution. Under current Rule 11.1(a)(1), the Exchange does not accept Market Orders, other than those with a Time-in-Force (``TIF'') instruction of Regular Hours Only or a Stop Price, prior to 4:00 a.m. Eastern Time or prior to 7:00 a.m. Eastern Time for orders eligible for a 7:00 a.m. Start. As part of the Exchange's transition to trading 23 hours per day, 5 days per week (``23x5 Trading''), the Exchange updated Rule 11.1(a) to introduce a new subparagraph (3) titled ``Orders Permitted in Each Session.'' Rule 11.1(a)(3), which is approved but not yet effective, states: ``Market Orders, other than those designated with a Time-in-Force instruction of Regular Hours Only or those that include a Stop Price, will not be accepted by the Exchange prior to Regular Trading Hours.'' The intent of this sentence was to prevent Market Orders from executing during the Overnight Trading Session and the Pre-Opening Session, but the text did not expressly prohibit the Exchange from accepting Market Orders during Regular Trading Hours and executing during the Post-Closing Session, which experiences similar characteristics regarding liquidity and volume as the current Early Trading Session. Now, the Exchange proposes to add an additional sentence to the end of Rule 11.1(a)(3) which states: ``Orders without a limit price will not be eligible for execution outside of Regular Trading Hours.'' The addition of this sentence eliminates any potential ambiguity about when an order that does not contain a limit price will be eligible for execution on the Exchange. In addition, this proposed change is substantially similar to limits on unpriced orders currently in place on Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (``Nasdaq'') and NYSE Arca, Inc. (``NYSE Arca'') and differs only in that the Exchange's proposed rule refers to orders without a limit price rather than specifically designating market orders or pegged orders as other market centers have done in their rule text. The Exchange also proposes to amend Rule 11.6(q)(2) to clarify that a Day Order entered during the Order Acceptance Queueing Time or Overnight Trading Session will expire at the end of Regular Trading Hours on the same business day to which the Overnight Trading Session belongs, as provided in Rule 11.1(b). This amendment replaces the phrase ``following trading day,'' which could be read ambiguously for orders entered after midnight during the Overnight Trading Session, with language that expressly ties the order's expiration to the business day to which the Overnight Trading Session belongs. The change is consistent with the Exchange's intent as described in the Original Filing, which introduced the 23x5 Trading framework and explained that ``a trading day is deemed to begin at 9:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the preceding calendar day.'' Under Rule 11.1(b), a business day includes the Overnight Trading Session on the preceding calendar day, meaning the entire Overnight Trading Session (from 9:00 p.m. through 4:00 a.m.) belongs to the following business day. The proposed amendment merely conforms the Day Order TIF definition to this structural principle and does not alter any operational aspect of Day Order handling. Specifically, current Rule 11.6(q)(2) provides that a Day Order entered during the Order Acceptance Queueing Time or the Overnight Trading Session ``will expire at the end of Regular Trading Hours on the following trading day.'' The Exchange proposes to replace ``following trading day'' with ``same business day to which the Overnight Trading Session belongs, as provided in Rule 11.1(b).'' This revision eliminates any potential ambiguity regarding whether an order entered after midnight i.e., during the portion of the Overnight Trading Session occurring on a new calendar day) could be interpreted as expiring on a different business day than intended. This proposed rule change will become operative in conjunction with the Original Filing. Rules 11.1(a)(3) and 11.6(q)(2) will be amended with the approved rule text in the Original Filing, whereby the Exchange seeks to offer a new Overnight Trading Session. The amended rule text will take effect in December 2026 pending industry readiness. Prior to codifying the amended rule text, the Exchange will file a proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Exchange Act and the rules thereunder to amend its rules confirming that the Exchange is able to comply with its obligations under the Exchange Act and the rules thereunder during the Overnight Trading Session and that the Equity Data Plans are prepared to collect, consolidate, process and disseminate quotation and transaction information at all times during the Overnight Trading Session. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Fees Schedule
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Fees Schedule

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend its Fees Schedule, effective October 1, 2026, to (1) amend the Binary Options rate table to replace the fixed, premium-based transaction fees currently applicable to XSPBX options with a tier-based constant transaction fee methodology applicable to Index Binaries for Customer, Clearing Trading Permit Holder Proprietary, Broker-Dealer (including Joint Back-Office, Non-Trading Permit Holder Market Maker, and Professional), and Cboe Options Market-Maker/DPM/LMM orders executed electronically and removing liquidity, while retaining the existing per-contract transaction fees for Cboe Options Market-Maker/DPM/LMM liquidity-adding and manual orders, together with new footnote 55; and (2) add IEX to fee code RD within the Routing Fees section of the Fees Schedule. Index Binaries Transaction Fees The Fees Schedule currently includes a Rate Table--Binary Options, which sets forth transaction fees for XSPBX options. The current table assesses fixed per-contract transaction fees that vary by capacity and across seven premium ranges (less than $0.04; $0.04-$0.09; $0.10-$0.24; $0.25-$0.75; $0.76-$0.90; $0.91-$0.96; and greater than $0.96). Specifically, Customer orders are assessed $0.04 (fee code D1), $0.08 (fee code D2), $0.20 (fee code D3), and $0.30 (fee code D4) per contract, with the fee increasing as the premium approaches $0.50 and decreasing symmetrically as the premium approaches $0.00 or $1.00. Clearing Trading Permit Holder Proprietary and Broker- Dealer orders (including Joint Back-Office, Non-Trading Permit Holder Market Maker, and Professional orders) are assessed $0.10 (fee code N1), $0.15 (fee code N2), $0.25 (fee code N3), and $0.35 (fee code N4) per contract across the same premium ranges. Cboe Options Market-Maker/DPM/LMM orders are assessed $0.10 (fee code H1), $0.15 (fee code H2), $0.25 (fee code H3), and $0.35 (fee code H4) per contract across the same premium ranges when executed electronically and taking liquidity, $0.05 per contract (fee code HA) when executed electronically and adding liquidity, and $0.15 per contract (fee code HM) when executed manually. The Exchange proposes to amend the Rate Table--Binary Options to replace the fixed, premium-based transaction fees currently applicable to XSPBX options with a tier-based constant transaction fee methodology applicable to ``Index Binaries,'' under which transaction fees for Customer, Clearing Trading Permit Holder Proprietary, Broker-Dealer (including Joint Back-Office, Non-Trading Permit Holder Market Maker, and Professional), and Cboe Options Market-Maker/DPM/LMM orders executed electronically and removing liquidity, will be calculated using the following formula: Transaction Fee = ((k*p*(1-p)*c)*m) where k is the tier-based constant for the applicable capacity; p is the contract price ($0.01-$1.00); c is the number of contracts traded; and m is the contract multiplier (i.e., 100). The proposed tier-based constants (k) are as follows: Customer (capacity code C): 1.2% (fee code HC); Clearing Trading Permit Holder Proprietary, Broker-Dealer, Joint Back-Office, Non-Trading Permit Holder Market Maker, and Professional (capacity codes F, L, B, N, U, and J): 1.4% (fee code HD); and Cboe Options Market-Maker/DPM/LMM (capacity code M), Electronic, Removing Liquidity: 1.4% (fee code HB). Cboe Options Market-Maker/DPM/LMM orders executed electronically and adding liquidity and executed manually will continue to be assessed flat per-contract transaction fees of $0.05 (fee code HA) and $0.15 (fee code HM), respectively, which are unchanged from the current fees. The Exchange believes it is reasonable to continue to assess these orders flat per-contract fees rather than fees under the proposed price-based methodology because Market-Makers, DPMs, and LMMs, unlike other market participants, are subject to continuous quoting and other obligations under the Exchange's Rules that require them to provide liquidity across the full range of contract prices, including in contracts priced near $0.50, where the proposed methodology would otherwise result in the highest fees. A flat, low per-contract fee for liquidity-adding electronic executions and manual executions provides Market-Makers, DPMs, and LMMs with fee certainty that does not vary with the price at which they are obligated to quote, which the Exchange believes encourages them to continue to provide tighter and deeper markets in Index Binaries, to the benefit of all market participants. Market-Maker/DPM/LMM electronic orders that remove liquidity do not further these obligations in the same manner and will therefore be subject to the proposed methodology (fee code HB), consistent with other non-Customer capacities. Maintaining the current flat fees for liquidity-adding and manual Market-Maker/DPM/LMM executions also avoids any fee increase for these participants as a result of the proposed change. The Exchange also proposes to adopt new footnote 55, which provides that ``Index Binaries include XSPBX,'' and to append footnote 55 to each ``Index Binaries'' product designation in the new rate table. XSPBX will therefore continue to be the only binary option subject to the rate table following the proposed change. Under the proposed methodology, the transaction fee for an Index Binary is a function of p*(1-p), which is greatest when the contract price is $0.50 and declines symmetrically as the contract price approaches $0.00 or $1.00. The proposed methodology therefore preserves the general shape of the current premium-range fee structure, under which the highest fees apply to contracts priced near $0.50 and the lowest fees apply to contracts priced near $0.00 or $1.00, while replacing seven discrete premium ranges with a continuous calculation based on the actual contract price. On August 13, 2026, NYSE Texas, Inc. (``NYSE Texas'' or the ``Exchange'') filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the ``Commission''), pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (``Act'') and Rule 19b-4 thereunder, a proposed rule change to adopt new Rule 24 under Article 22 of the NYSE Texas Rule Book to offer certain issuers complimentary products and services from the Exchange. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 5.33(g) and Rule 5.34
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 5.33(g) and Rule 5.34

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 5.33, which governs the trading of complex orders. The proposed additions to Rule 5.33(g)(6) would establish a related group framework under which a complex order consisting of legs in different groups of series in the class may Leg into the Simple Book, in addition to being posted to the COB, if the Exchange has designated those groups as a related group and the other applicable legging restrictions that are currently enumerated under Rule 5.33 are satisfied. Additionally, the Exchange also proposes to add interpretative guidance under Rule 5.34 to establish that, when the Exchange sets parameters for risk controls on a group basis, that the Exchange (or Users, when applicable) may also set parameters for a related group. Background Currently, the Exchange has authority under Rule 4.13(f) to list SPX or VIX on a group basis. The Exchange currently lists SPX on a group basis; specifically, the Exchange lists A.M.-settled SPX options under the symbol SPX and lists P.M.-settled SPX options under the symbol SPXW. While SPX and SPXW options are part of the same S&P 500 Index options class, the Exchange may apply different trading parameters to SPXW options than those it applies to SPX options (pursuant to Rule 1.5). SPX options reside on one matching engine while SPXW is on a separate matching engine. The Exchange intends to launch Weekly A.M.-settled SPX options (``SPXO'') and list SPXO options as a separate group from both SPX and SPXW. However, SPXO and SPX options will both be on the same matching engine. Legging Under Rule 5.33(g) (``Legging''), a complex order may execute against orders and quotes resting in the Simple Book (pursuant to subparagraphs (d)(5)(A) and (e)) if it can execute in full or in a permissible ratio and has no more than the maximum number of legs, as the Exchange determines on a class-by-class basis, and is subject to a list of restrictions. Specifically, one such restriction under Rule 5.33(g)(6) states that ``[i]f the Exchange determines to list SPX or VIX on a group basis pursuant to Rule 4.13, a complex order consisting of legs in different groups of series in the class may not Leg into the Simple Book. A complex order consisting of legs in the same group of series may Leg, subject to the other restrictions in this paragraph (g).'' Pursuant to this provision, a complex order that consists of SPX and SPXW option legs is currently unable to leg into each underlying leg's Simple Book. The primary reason for this provision is because the Simple Books for SPX and SPXW are on different matching engines, as noted above. However, SPXO options will be on the same matching engine as SPX options. As a result, Exchange technology will allow complex orders comprised of legs from these two different groups (SPXO and SPX) to leg into their respective Simple Books. Complex orders that include an SPX or SPXO leg and an SPXW leg will continue to not be able to leg into their respective Simple Books. In order to account for this, the Exchange proposes to add the related group framework to Rule 5.33(g)(6) so that a complex order consisting of legs in different groups of series in the class that Cboe has designated as related groups may Leg into the Simple Book, in addition to being posted to the COB. The proposed related group framework reflects the current technological limitations of the Exchange's system. The Exchange will announce groups designated as related groups via Exchange Notice. The proposed change does not alter the existing Legging restrictions in Rule 5.33(g); rather, it adds a framework under proposed paragraph (g)(6) for the Exchange to designate groups as related, and thus permit complex orders comprised of legs from different groups to leg into their respective Simple Books, if Exchange technology can accommodate legging of complex orders comprised of legs for different groups. Because the Exchange remains unable to leg complex orders comprised of legs for groups that reside on different matching engines, only groups whose relevant series are processed by the same matching engine may be eligible for designation as a related group. Risk Controls Currently, Rule 1.5(c) grants the Exchange authority to set trading parameters on a group basis if parameters are set on a class-by-class basis and the Exchange determines to list SPX or VIX on a group basis pursuant to Rule 4.13. Rule 5.34 allows the Exchange to set several limits on a class by class basis. Under current Rule 1.5, the Exchange has authority to set those parameters on a group basis when SPX or VIX is listed on a group basis. Self-Regulatory Organizations; Long-Term Stock Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Modify Listing Rules Regarding Dually-Listed Securities

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to adopt Supplementary Material .02 to Rule 14.210 (Dually-Listed Securities) to specify that all companies listing securities on LTSE must be listed on another registered national securities exchange (``Supplementary Material .02''). While LTSE maintains primary listing standards in its Rulebook and intends to operate as a primary listing market in the future, LTSE currently lists only issuers that also maintain a primary listing on another national securities exchange. The proposed rule text does not modify or eliminate LTSE's underlying initial or continued listing standards; instead, it clarifies the relationship between those standards and LTSE's current listing model for dually listed issuers. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the provisions of Section 6 of the Act, in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act, in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change promotes just and equitable principles of trade and protects investors by providing clear and transparent rules regarding LTSE's current listing model. Although LTSE maintains comprehensive primary listing standards within its Rulebook, LTSE currently operates under a model where listed issuers maintain a dual listing on another registered national securities exchange. The Exchange believes that codifying this requirement in proposed Supplementary Material .02 ensures that issuers, investors, and market participants have clarity regarding the requisite dual-listing status for LTSE-listed securities. By eliminating potential ambiguity surrounding LTSE's current listing operations, the proposed rule change prevents confusion in the marketplace and ensures that all market participants operate with a shared, precise understanding of LTSE's dual-listing framework. Importantly, the proposed rule text does not modify, relax, or eliminate LTSE's existing initial or continued listing standards. Instead, it simply clarifies the practical application of those standards in relation to LTSE's present operating model. By preserving underlying quality and governance benchmarks while harmonizing rule text with operational reality, the Exchange maintains high listing standards that promote market integrity without disrupting existing trading mechanisms or regulatory oversight across the national market system. The mandatory dual-listing requirement under Supplementary Material .02 will apply uniformly to all issuers listing securities on LTSE. Furthermore, the proposed rule change is identical in substance to existing rules previously approved or adopted by other self-regulatory organizations. Specifically, the proposed rule text mirrors Nasdaq Texas, LLC (``Nasdaq TX'') IM-5220-1, which similarly requires all companies listing on that exchange to maintain a dual-listing on another national securities exchange. Adopting an identical approach establishes regulatory consistency across listing venues. B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change fosters intermarket competition by clarifying the parameters under which issuers may list on LTSE while maintaining their primary listings elsewhere. Because the rule is substantively identical to Nasdaq Texas IM-5220-1, it ensures a level playing field among national securities exchanges that operate dual-listing structures. The proposed rule will apply equally to all issuers listing securities on LTSE. Because the proposed rule merely codifies current operational practice and explicitly preserves the Exchange's underlying listing standards, it imposes no unexpected burdens on issuers or market participants while fostering fair and open competition within the national market system. C. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 19.3 and Rule 19.4 To Establish Generic Listing Criteria and Continued Listing Standards for Options on Commodity-Based Trusts Holding Multiple Crypto Assets and To Permit the Listing of Options on Exchange-Traded Funds

Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 19.3 and Rule 19.4 To Establish Generic Listing Criteria and Continued Listing Standards for Options on Commodity-Based Trusts Holding Multiple Crypto Assets and To Permit the Listing of Options on Exchange-Traded Funds

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 19.3 (Criteria for Underlying Securities) and Rule 19.4 (Withdrawal of Approval of Underlying Securities) to (i) establish listing criteria and continued listing standards for options on shares of commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets, (ii) update Rule 19.3(i)(1) to permit the listing of options on an exchange traded fund as defined in Rule 6c-11 under the Investment Company Act of 1940 (``Rule 6c-11''), and (iii) make conforming amendments to remove individual product-specific references and update cross-references within the rules. Background The Exchange's existing rules permit the listing and trading of options on various types of exchange-traded products, including options on shares of exchange-traded funds (``ETFs''), commodity pool ETFs, currency trust shares, and commodity-based trusts holding a single crypto asset. Specifically, Rule 19.3(i) sets forth the criteria for securities deemed appropriate for options trading, including Fund Shares that are principally traded on a national securities exchange and defined as an ``NMS stock'' under Rule 600 of Regulation NMS. Cboe Options Exchange, Inc. (``Cboe Options''), an affiliate of the Exchange, recently received approval from the Commission to list and trade options on commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets. Specifically, Cboe Options adopted Rules 4.3.06(a)(6) and 4.4.06(c) to establish initial and continued generic listing criteria for options on commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets. Additionally, Cboe Options amended Rule 4.3.06(a)(4) to remove individual product-specific references for crypto asset ETPs, and in a separate filing amended Rule 4.3.06(a)(1) to permit the listing of options on ETFs as defined in Rule 6c-11. Proposed Rule Changes The Exchange now proposes to adopt rules that are substantively identical to the Cboe Options Rules described above. Specifically, the Exchange proposes the following amendments. Amendments to Rule 19.3(i) The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 19.3(i) to establish generic listing criteria for options on commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets. Currently, Rule 19.3(i)(5) permits the listing of options on commodity-based trusts that hold a single crypto asset meeting certain requirements. The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 19.3(i)(5) to also permit the listing of options on commodity-based trusts that hold multiple crypto assets, provided that each underlying crypto asset held by such trust satisfies the following requirements: i. the total global supply of each underlying crypto asset held by the Commodity-Based Trust has an average daily market value of at least $700 million over the last 12 months; and ii. each crypto asset held by the Commodity-Based Trust underlies a derivatives contract that trades on a market with which the Exchange has a comprehensive surveillance sharing agreement, whether directly or through common membership in the Intermarket Surveillance Group (``ISG''). These requirements are designed to ensure that each crypto asset underlying options approved for trading on the Exchange has sufficient market capitalization and is subject to adequate market surveillance. These criteria are substantively identical to those approved by the Commission for Cboe Options. In addition, the Exchange proposes to update Rule 19.3(i)(1) to permit the listing of options on exchange traded funds as defined in Rule 6c-11, portfolio depositary receipts, or index fund shares. Proposed Rule 19.3(i)(1) is substantively identical to Cboe Rule 4.3.06(a)(1). The requirements of Rule 19.3(i)(1) are generally based on the generic listing standards for exchange-traded funds that pre- dated the adoption of Rule 6c-11. The Exchange proposes to eliminate the language from the rule text that specifies the securities and/or financial instruments that the entity holds and instead provide that the securities deemed appropriate for options trading shall include shares or other securities (``Fund Shares''), including but not limited to Partnership Units as defined in this Rule, that are principally traded on a national securities exchange and are defined as an ``NMS stock'' under Rule 600 of Regulation NMS, and that are listed pursuant to generic listing standards for an exchange-traded fund as defined in Rule 6c-11, portfolio depositary receipts, or index fund shares. In 2019, the Commission adopted Rule 6c-11 to permit exchange- traded funds that satisfy certain conditions to operate without obtaining an exemptive order from the Commission under the Investment Company Act of 1940. In 2020, the Commission approved generic listing standards pursuant to Rule 19b-4(e) of the Exchange Act for exchange-traded funds that meet the requirements of Rule 6c-11 (i.e., ETF Shares). The Commission found that the ETF Shares generic listing standards are reasonably designed to help prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices particularly because a central qualification for listing generically is ongoing compliance with Rule 6c-11, which requires, among other things, ETF Shares to prominently disclose the portfolio holdings that will form the basis for each calculation of net asset value per share. The Commission stated that it believes that such portfolio transparency should help prevent manipulation of the price of ETF Shares. The Exchange believes this same transparency rationale supports the generic listing of options on ETF Shares by aligning the options generic listing standards with the ETF Shares generic listing standards. This proposal simply creates a streamlined pathway for listing options on qualifying ETF Shares that meet the enhanced transparency standards under Rule 6c-11. The Exchange believes this proposed listing standard for options on ETF Shares is reasonable and will result in options that are not readily susceptible to manipulation in light of existing Rule 6c-11 transparency requireme

Self-Regulatory Organizations; New York Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Harmonize NYSE Rule 3220 With Certain Changes by FINRA

1. Purpose This proposed rule change is based on a filing recently submitted by FINRA, and approved by the Commission, to amend FINRA Rule 3220 (Influencing or Rewarding Employees of Others), and is intended to harmonize the Exchange's rules with those of FINRA so as to promote uniform standards across the securities industry. The Exchange proposes to harmonize NYSE Rule 3220 (Influencing or Rewarding Employees of Others) with certain changes by FINRA to FINRA Rule 3220 to increase the gift limit from $100 to $300. Additionally, unlike FINRA Rule 3220, current NYSE Rule 3220 does not include provisions covering: supervision and recordkeeping; gifts incidental to business entertainment; valuation of gifts; aggregation of gifts; personal gifts; bereavement gifts; de minimis gifts and promotional or commemorative items; donations due to federally declared major disasters; or gifts to a member or member organization's associated persons or individual retail customers. To further harmonize its rules with FINRA, the Exchange proposes to adopt these provisions in proposed Supplementary Material .01 through .09 to NYSE Rule 3220 that is substantially similar to Supplementary Material .01 through .09 to FINRA Rule 3220 adopted in the FINRA Rule Change. Pursuant to Rule 17d-2 under the Act, the Exchange and FINRA have entered into an agreement to allocate regulatory responsibility for common rules (the ``17d-2 Agreement''). The 17d-2 Agreement covers common members of the Exchange and FINRA and allocates to FINRA regulatory responsibility, with respect to common members, for the following: (i) examination of common members of the Exchange and FINRA for compliance with certain federal securities laws, rules and regulations and rules of the Exchange that the Exchange has certified as identical or substantially similar to FINRA rules; (ii) investigation of common members of the Exchange and FINRA for violations of certain federal securities laws, rules or regulations, or Exchange rules that the Exchange has certified as identical or substantially similar to a FINRA rule; and (iii) enforcement of compliance by common members with certain federal securities laws, rules and regulations, and the rules of the Exchange that the Exchange has certified as identical or substantially similar to FINRA rules. NYSE Rule 3220 is based on FINRA Rule 3220. NYSE Rule 3220(a) states that no member, member organization, or person associated with a member organization, shall, directly or indirectly, give or permit to be given anything of value, including gratuities, in excess of one hundred dollars per individual per year to any person, principal, proprietor, employee, agent to representative of another person where such payment or gratuity is in relation to the business of the employer of the recipient of the payment or gratuity. NYSE Rule 3220(b) provides for certain exceptions from the requirements enumerated in Rule 3220(a). Finally, NYSE Rule 3220(c) requires a member or member organization to maintain a record of payments or gratuities of any amount for a specified period of time. The Exchange believes that harmonizing NYSE Rule 3220 with FINRA Rule 3220 will help to avoid confusion among Exchange members and member organizations that are also members of FINRA. The proposed changes to NYSE Rule 3220 are also designed to enable the Exchange to incorporate the entirety of NYSE Rule 3220 in the 17d-2 Agreement, further reducing duplicative regulation of members and member organizations that are also members of FINRA. For the avoidance of doubt, NYSE Rule 3220 would equally apply to Exchange-only members and member organizations as the Exchange believes it appropriately protects against improprieties, such as conflicts of interest, that might arise when a member or member organization or person associated with a member organization gives items of value to an employee of another person, such as an institutional customer, vendor or counterparty with the hope of strengthening the relationship with the customer. As amended, like FINRA Rule 3220(a), paragraph (a) of NYSE Rule 3220 would prohibit gifts in excess of $300 per individual per year where the gift or gratuity is in relation to the business of the employer of the recipient. Additionally, the Exchange proposes to adopt Supplementary Material .01 through .09 to NYSE Rule 3220 to codify the provisions within FINRA Supplementary Materials 3220.01 through 3220.09. More specifically, proposed Supplementary Material .01 through .09 to NYSE Rule 3220, like FINRA Supplementary Materials 3220.01 through 3220.09, would codify the FINRA Supplementary Materials to Rule 3220 related to gifts incidental to business entertainment, valuation of gifts, aggregation of gifts, personal gifts, bereavement gifts, de minimis gifts and promotional or commemorative items, donations due to federally declared major disasters, supervision and recordkeeping, and gifts to a Member's or Member Organization's associated persons or individual retail customers. Proposed Supplementary Material .01 (Gifts Incidental to Business Entertainment) would state that a gift given during the course of a business entertainment event is subject to Rule 3220 unless it is consistent with the requirements of proposed Supplementary Material .04 (Personal Gifts) or .06 (De Minimis Gifts and Promotional or Commemorative Items) which is substantially similar to FINRA Rule 3220 Supplementary Material .04 and .06. For the purpose of the $300 limit, the cost of the business entertainment event itself would not be included in the value of the gift. Proposed Supplementary Material .02 (Valuation of Gifts) would require members and member organizations to value gifts (other than tickets for sporting or other events) at cost, exclusive of tax and delivery charges, and would require members and member organizations to value tickets for sporting or other events at the higher of cost or face value. (``PRA''), the Securities and Exchange Commission (``SEC'' or ``Commission'') is submitting to the Office of Management and Budget (``OMB'') this request for the extension and approval of the mandatory collection of information related to the registration of municipal advisors provided for in Rules 15Ba1-1 to 15Ba1-8 (17 CFR 240.15Ba1-1 to 17 CFR 240.15Ba1-8) and Forms MA (17 CFR 249.1300), MA-I (17 CFR 249.1310), MA-W (17 CFR 249.1320), and MA-NR (17 CFR 249.1330) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78a et seq.) (the ``Exchange Act''). The required Federal Register notice with a 60-day comment period soliciting comments on this collection of information was published. In 2010, the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (``Dodd-Frank Act'') amended Section 15B of the Exchange Act to require a new class of regulated persons, ``municipal advisors,'' to register with the Commission. Section 15B(a)(1)(B) of the Exchange Act, as added by the Dodd-Frank Act, makes it unlawful for a municipal advisor to provide advice to or on behalf of a municipal entity or obligated person with respect to municipal financial products or the issuance of municipal securities, or to undertake certain solicitations of a municipal entity or obligated person, unless the municipal advisor is registered with the Commission. On September 20, 2013, the Commission adopted Rules 15Ba1-1 through 15Ba1-8 and Rule 15Bc4-1 under the Exchange Act to establish the rules by which a municipal advisor must obtain, maintain, and terminate its registration with the Commission. The rules, among other things: (i) require municipal advisors to file Forms MA, MA-I, MA-W, and MA-NR with the Commission to obtain, maintain, or terminate their registration with the Commission, (ii) require municipal advisors to maintain certain books and records in accordance with the Exchange Act, (iii) interpret the definition of the term ``municipal advisor,'' (iv) interpret the statutory exclusions to that definition, and (v) provide certain additional regulatory exemptions. The rules became effective on January 13, 2014; however, on January 13, 2014, the Commission temporarily stayed such rules until July 1, 2014. Amendments to Forms MA and MA-I designed to eliminate aspects of the forms that request filers to provide certain forms of personally identifiable information of natural persons, including Social Security numbers, dates of birth, and foreign identity numbers became effective on May 14, 2018. I. Forms MA and MA-I Rule 15Ba1-2 requires each person applying for registration with the Commission as a municipal advisor to file electronically with the Commission Form MA and, with respect to each natural person associated with the municipal advisory firm who engages in municipal advisory activities on its behalf, Form MA-I. Although much of the information required by Form MA is already publicly available with respect to municipal advisors that are already registered with the Commission as investment advisers or broker-dealers, many municipal advisors that are not currently registered with the Commission in another capacity will make this information available for the first time. title: A23. What are the record retention requirements for Industry Member CAT Reporters?
raw_text:
A23. What are the record retention requirements for Industry Member CAT Reporters?

According to each of the Participant’s CAT compliance rules, information required to be reported to the CAT must be maintained in accordance with SEC Rule 17a-4(b). This rule states that these records must be preserved for at least three years, the first two years in an accessible place. Records are not required to be retained in an electronic format; they may be retained in a paper format. However, with respect to Business Clock synchronization logs, such logs must include synchronization results for a period of not less than five years ending on the then current date, or for the entire period for which the Industry Member has been required to comply with this requirement if less than five years.
