title: Cboe Clear U.S., LLC; Order Granting an Application, as Amended, for Temporary Registration as a Clearing Agency Under Section 17A of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934
raw_text:
Cboe Clear U.S., LLC; Order Granting an Application, as Amended, for Temporary Registration as a Clearing Agency Under Section 17A of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934

I. Introduction On June 30, 2026, Cboe Clear U.S., LLC (``CCUS'') filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (``Commission'') an application on Form CA-1 under Section 17A of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (``Exchange Act'') seeking to register as a clearing agency to provide central counterparty (``CCP'') services for binary options that are securities. In its application, CCUS requests temporary registration as a clearing agency under Section 17A(b) of the Exchange Act and pursuant to 17 CFR 240.17ab2-1 (``Rule 17Ab2-1''). Notice of the application (``Notice'') was published for comment in the Federal Register on July 24, 2026. CCUS amended its application on July 7 and 17, August 18, September 4, and October 1, 2026 (as amended, ``Application''). The Commission received one comment letter, as well as a response from CCUS. The comment letter supports approval of CCUS's request for temporary registration as a ``stopgap;'' as to permanent registration, it raises concerns as to the risk of vertically integrated solutions and requests that the Commission consider the capital costs and risks of a more fragmented clearing structure. The comment letter received, and CCUS's response thereto, are discussed in Parts III and IV. This order grants CCUS's request for temporary registration as a clearing agency with an exemption from certain requirements as to which the Commission is directed to make a determination under Sections 17A(b)(3)(B) and (F) for a period of 18 months from the date of this order, for the reasons set forth in Parts III and IV below. II. Statutory Standard for Registration as a Clearing Agency Clearing agencies are broadly defined under the Exchange Act and undertake a variety of functions, including providing the services of a CCP. Pursuant to Section 17A of the Exchange Act and Rule 17Ab2-1 thereunder, an entity that meets the definition of a clearing agency must register with the Commission. Section 17A(b)(1) also states that, upon the Commission's motion or upon a clearing agency's application, the Commission may conditionally or unconditionally exempt a clearing agency from any provisions of Section 17A or the rules or regulations thereunder if the Commission finds that such exemption is consistent with the public interest, the protection of investors, and the purposes of Section 17A, including the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions and the safeguarding of securities and funds. In addition to the requirements set forth in Rule 17Ab2-1, Section 19(a)(1) of the Exchange Act establishes the standard for Commission review of an application for registration as a clearing agency. Pursuant thereto, the Commission shall grant registration of a clearing agency if it finds that the requirements of the Exchange Act and the rules and regulations thereunder with respect to the applicant are satisfied. The Commission shall deny such registration if it does not make such finding. The requirements of the Exchange Act applicable to clearing agencies are set forth in Section 17A and the rules and regulations thereunder. Accordingly, to grant CCUS's Application for registration as a clearing agency, the Commission must find that the Application satisfies the requirements of Section 17A(b) of the Exchange Act and rules and regulations thereunder, including the determinations set forth in paragraphs (A) through (I) of Section 17A(b)(3) of the Exchange Act. Pursuant to Rule 17Ab2-1(c), the Commission, upon the request of a clearing agency, may grant registration of the clearing agency but exempt the registrant from one or more of the requirements as to which the Commission is directed to make a determination pursuant to Section 17A(b)(3) of the Exchange Act, provided that any such registration shall be effective only for eighteen months from the date the registration is made effective (or such longer period as the Commission may provide by order). After a clearing agency's application for registration is granted, the clearing agency must continue to satisfy the requirements of the Exchange Act and the rules and regulations thereunder. In the context of temporary registration, the clearing agency must satisfy the requirements of the Exchange Act and the rules and regulations thereunder, except as to requirements, rules, or regulations to which an exemption has been provided. The Commission has explained that ``[a]n approval of clearing agency registration does not mean that no further modifications of the applicant's rules, systems, procedures, or practices are needed.'' Rather, the Commission stated that a registered clearing agency's obligation to continue to satisfy the requirements of the Exchange Act and the rules and regulations thereunder means that ``[t]he self-regulatory obligations of [a] fully registered clearing agenc[y] cannot end'' after registration. To ensure such compliance, the Commission stated that it ``will continue to use its oversight, inspection, and enforcement authority as necessary and appropriate to further the purposes of the [Exchange] Act.'' III. Review of Application Under Statutory Standard for Registration Consistent with the requirements in Sections 17A and 19(a)(1) of the Exchange Act described above, the Commission below analyzes the Application against each of the statutory requirements under Section 17A(b)(3)(A) through (I) to be registered as a clearing agency. title: Order Under Section 36 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 Granting Conditional Exemptive Relief Regarding the Treatment of Customer Margin Under Item 13 and Note F of Exhibit A to Rule 15c3-3
raw_text:
Order Under Section 36 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 Granting Conditional Exemptive Relief Regarding the Treatment of Customer Margin Under Item 13 and Note F of Exhibit A to Rule 15c3-3

I. Introduction A. Overview of the Exemptive Order On September 18, 2026, Cboe Clear U.S., LLC (``CCUS''), a clearing agency now temporarily registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (``Commission'') pursuant to Rule 17Ab2-1(c) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (``Exchange Act'') for a period of 18 months, filed an application with the Commission (``Application'') to obtain an exemption pursuant to section 36(a)(1) of the Exchange Act, in accordance with the procedures set forth in Exchange Act Rule 0-12. Specifically, CCUS requested exemptive relief on behalf of broker-dealers that are CCUS clearing members (``Clearing Members'') from the limitation in Item 13 and Note F of Exhibit A to Rule 15c3-3 that confines the Item 13 debit to the amount of margin required and on deposit with the Options Clearing Corporation (``OCC'') for all option contracts written or purchased in customer accounts. This would afford Clearing Members the same treatment for margin required and on deposit at CCUS for purposes of the reserve computation requirements under Item 13 and Note F of Rule 15c3-3a as is currently afforded to margin required and on deposit with the OCC. On September 25, 2026, the Commission published a notice of an application for an exemption and requested comment regarding the Application and the proposed conditions set forth therein. The Notice was published in the Federal Register on September 29, 2026. The Commission received one comment on the Notice of an Application. For the reasons discussed below, this order grants Clearing Members conditional exemptive relief from the limitation in Item 13 and Note F of 15c3-3a that confines the Item 13 debit to margin required and on deposit with the OCC for all option contracts written or purchased in customer accounts. B. Overview of Rule 15c3-3 and Rule 15c3-3a Rule 15c3-3, the broker-dealer customer protection rule, requires, among other things, broker-dealers that hold customer cash and securities (``carrying broker-dealers'') to compute the net amount of cash owed to customers under a formula in Rule 15c3-3a (``customer reserve computation''). Generally, carrying broker-dealers must perform this customer reserve computation and make any required deposit into special reserve bank account daily or weekly. The rule also requires a carrying broker-dealer to perform a PAB reserve computation for the proprietary securities and cash it holds for other broker- dealers, known as proprietary accounts of broker-dealers (``PAB accounts''). Item 13 of the customer reserve computation in Rule 15c3-3a includes as a debit in the computation the amount of margin required and on deposit with OCC for all option contracts written or purchased in customer accounts. Note F to Item 13 states that Item 13 must include the amount of margin required and on deposit with the OCC to the extent such margin is represented by cash, proprietary qualified securities and letters of credit collateralized by customers' securities. Under that framework, the permitted debit is based on the margin amount posted by the broker-dealer to OCC that is calculated by OCC across all of the broker-dealer's customers with listed options (i.e., on an omnibus basis). C. Request for Exemptive Relief From CCUS In its Application, CCUS requested, pursuant to section 36(a)(1) of the Exchange Act, and in accordance with the procedures set forth in Rule 0-12, that the Commission issue an order exempting its Clearing Members from the limitation in Item 13 and Note F of Rule 15c3-3a that confines the Item 13 debit to the amount of margin required and on deposit with OCC for option contracts written or purchased in customer accounts. CCUS also requested that the exemptive relief apply with respect to the PAB reserve computation. In effect, CCUS is seeking comparable treatment for its Clearing Members under the customer reserve computation with respect to the margin that is required and on deposit at CCUS as has been afforded broker-dealers that are clearing members of OCC. In support of its request, CCUS stated that when the Commission adopted Item 13, and Note F thereto, OCC was the only clearing agency registered with the Commission to provide central counterparty services for securities options. CCUS stated that it does not believe that the Exchange Act requires or warrants different treatment for margin held on similar terms for security option products at different registered clearing agencies. Further, CCUS stated that section 17A(a)(2) of the Exchange Act directs the Commission, with due regard for the maintenance of fair competition among clearing agencies, to facilitate a national system for the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions and to assure equal regulation under the Exchange Act of registered clearing agencies. Consequently, CCUS stated that reading Item 13 to exclude margin held at a second registered options clearing agency because it did not exist when the rule was amended would be inconsistent with this statutory mandate. To further support its position, CCUS stated that Item 14 and Item 15 of the customer reserve computation do not name any particular clearing agency, and do not distinguish between registered clearing agencies. CCUS stated that where the Commission anticipated that more than one clearing agency could hold margin, it framed the customer reserve computation treatment of such margin by reference to a registered category rather than name a specific existing clearing agency. Consequently, CCUS stated that permitting broker- dealers to treat margin held at other registered clearing agencies would treat functionally equivalent margin on equivalent terms. Additionally, CCUS stated that its proposed rules contemplate customer protection standards that satisfy the same regulatory requirements as those under which OCC operates. Self-Regulatory Organizations; MEMX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 11.15 (Clearly Erroneous Executions)

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 11.15 (``Clearly Erroneous Executions'') in light of the Commission's approval of Overnight Protected Bands under the LULD Plan for 23/5 Trading. Background In September 2026, the Exchange filed for immediate effectiveness a proposal to introduce trading 23 hours a day, 5 days a week (``23/5 Trading''). As part of that proposal, the Exchange made changes to Rule 11.15 (``Clearly Erroneous Executions'') to treat transactions executed during the Overnight Trading Session in the same manner as transactions executed during the Pre-Market and Post-Market Sessions. Subsequently, the Operating Committee of the Plan to Address Extraordinary Market Volatility (``LULD Plan'') filed proposed Amendment 27 to the LULD Plan, which proposed to establish price band protections during overnight trading hours (``Overnight Price Bands''). The Operating Committee proposed that the Overnight Price Bands would initially be temporary static bands 20% above and below two reference points, and that after implementation, the Operating Committee would evaluate the performance of such Overnight Price Bands and propose appropriate changes in a new plan amendment. On August 5, 2026, the Commission approved the proposal. In light of the Commission's approval of these changes to the LULD Plan, the Exchange now proposes to reverse the changes to Rule 11.15 that were made as part of the MEMX 23/5 Filing, and to make several other amendments to Rule 11.15 in light of the Commission's approval of Overnight Price Bands. In general, Rule 11.15 describes the process a market participant may use to request cancellation of a transaction that was ``clearly erroneous.'' The current rule's central premise is that if LULD Price Bands under the LULD Plan were available and correct at the time the transaction was executed, the transaction is not eligible for clearly erroneous review. Specifically, Rule 11.15(c)(1) currently provides that ``[i]f the execution time of the transaction(s) under review is during Regular Trading Hours, the transaction will not be reviewable as clearly erroneous'' except in certain limited circumstances, including when (A) the transaction is in an NMS stock that is not subject to the LULD Plan (e.g., rights and warrants), (B) the transaction was executed at a time when LULD Price Bands were unavailable or trading should have been prevented due to a regulatory halt or other halt, or (C) several other limited circumstances. In approving the existing version of the rule, the Commission noted that restricting clearly erroneous review in this way during times when LULD Price Bands were in effect was ``consistent with the Act and will further the goal of providing greater certainty to market participants that trades executed within the Price Bands will stand and not be broken. . . . Thus, the proposal is designed to limit the potential discordance between the LULD mechanism and CEE review process.'' Currently, LULD Price Bands are available only during Regular Trading Hours, meaning that the restrictions on clearly erroneous review described above apply only during Regular Trading Hours. With the introduction of Overnight Price Bands, the Exchange now proposes to extend the existing restrictions on clearly erroneous review to the period when Overnight Price Bands are in place. This proposed change would be consistent with the Commission's rationale in approving the current version of the rule because it would limit any potential discordance between the LULD mechanism and CEE review in the overnight trading session, providing greater certainty to market participants that trades executed with the Overnight Price Bands will stand and not be broken. Reversal of Changes Made to Rule 11.15 As noted above, as part of the MEMX 23/5 Filing, the Exchange made changes to Rule 11.15 to treat transactions executed during the Overnight Trading Session in the same manner as transactions executed during the Pre-Market and Post-Market Sessions. Given the Commission's subsequent approval of Overnight Price Bands, the Exchange proposes to reverse each of the changes made to Rule 11.15 by the MEMX 23/5 Filing. As detailed below, this proposal would instead make clearly erroneous review of transactions executed during the Overnight Trading Session available in a manner similar to transactions executed during Regular Trading Hours. Proposed Changes to Rule 11.15(c)(1) To implement this change, the Exchange proposes to add several definitions to Rule 11.15(c)(1). First, the Exchange would add that the term ``LULD Protected Hours'' includes Regular Trading Hours and ``Overnight Protected Hours'' defined in Section VIII of the LULD Plan. Second, the Exchange would define ``LULD Price Bands'' or ``Price Bands'' to mean the Price Bands defined in Section V of the LULD Plan (i.e., the Price Bands that apply during Regular Trading Hours) and ``Overnight Price Bands'' as defined in Section VIII of the LULD Plan (i.e., the Price Bands that apply to the Overnight Protected Hours from 9:00 p.m. ET through 4:00 a.m. ET). The Exchange proposes to amend the current first sentence of Rule 11.15(c)(1) to replace the phrase ``Regular Trading Hours'' with ``LULD Protected Hours,'' to provide that ``[i]f the execution time of the transaction(s) under review is during LULD Protected Hours, the transaction will not be reviewable as clearly erroneous . . . .'' This change would extend the LULD-based restrictions on clearly erroneous review currently in place during Regular Trading Hours to the Overnight Protected Hours. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE Texas, Inc.; Notice of Filing of Amendment No. 1 and Order Granting Accelerated Approval of a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1, To Offer Complimentary Products and Services
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE Texas, Inc.; Notice of Filing of Amendment No. 1 and Order Granting Accelerated Approval of a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1, To Offer Complimentary Products and Services

I. Introduction On August 13, 2026, NYSE Texas, Inc. (``NYSE Texas'' or the ``Exchange'') filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the ``Commission''), pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (``Act'') and Rule 19b-4 thereunder, a proposed rule change to adopt new Rule 24 under Article 22 of the NYSE Texas Rule Book to offer certain issuers complimentary products and services from the Exchange. The proposed rule change was published for comment in the Federal Register on September 1, 2026. On October 5, 2026, the Exchange filed Amendment No. 1 to the proposed rule change, which replaced and superseded the original filing in its entirety. The Commission has received no comment letters on the proposal. The Commission is publishing this notice and order to solicit comments on Amendment No. 1 from interested persons and to approve the proposed rule change, as modified by Amendment No. 1, on an accelerated basis. II. Description of Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1 The Exchange is proposing to adopt Rule 24 under Article 22 of the NYSE Texas Rule Book to offer complimentary services to certain issuers listed on the Exchange. First, the Exchange proposes to codify in new Rule 24 that all issuers listed on the Exchange are entitled to certain services, including use of the Exchange's headquarters in Dallas, Texas, on a complimentary basis as described on the Exchange's website. The Exchange states that it offers these complimentary services to all issuers without regard to size or any other factor. Second, the Exchange proposes to define as an ``Eligible Dual Listing'' any U.S. or any non-U.S. company (i) whose primary class of equity securities is listed on another national securities exchange and is listing such class of securities on the Exchange as a dual listing pursuant to Rule 18 of the NYSE Texas Rule Book; and (ii) that has 160 million or more total shares of common stock issued and outstanding in all share classes, including and in addition to treasury shares (a non- U.S. company must have 160 million or more shares of an equity security issued and outstanding in the U.S). The Exchange will offer an Eligible Dual Listing a one-time package of visibility and investor engagement products and services with a commercial value of approximately $50,000. The Exchange states that the package of visibility and investor engagement products and services would entitle an Eligible Dual Listing to hold an investor meeting at the Exchange's headquarters in Dallas, Texas and a marketing activation to publicize the issuer's dual listing on the Exchange or other corporate developments. III. Discussion and Commission Findings After careful review, the Commission finds the proposed rule change, as modified by Amendment No. 1, is consistent with the requirements of Section 6 of the Act. Specifically, the Commission finds that the proposed rule change, as modified by Amendment No. 1, is consistent with Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act, in particular, in that the proposed rule is designed to provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among Exchange members, issuers, and other persons using the Exchange's facilities, and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. Moreover, the Commission finds that the proposed rule change, as modified by Amendment No. 1, is consistent with Section 6(b)(8) of the Act in that it does not impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposal to codify the Exchange's current offering of certain complimentary services to all issuers and to offer a one-time package of visibility and investor engagement products and services on a complimentary basis to certain issuers, as described above, is appropriate and consistent with the Act. Describing in the Exchange's rules the services available to listed companies, their associated values, and the length of time for which issuers are entitled to receive such services adds greater transparency to the Exchange's rules and will help to ensure that individual listed companies are not given specially negotiated packages of products or services to list, or remain listed, which would raise unfair discrimination issues under the Act. All listed companies will receive the complimentary services, including the use of the Exchange's headquarters, described on the Exchange's website. Further, the Exchange represents that offering the proposed complimentary services will not adversely affect the funding available for the Exchange's regulatory responsibilities. Accordingly, the Exchange will continue to be able to allocate sufficient resources to, and fully perform, all its regulatory obligations. Section 6(b)(5) of the Act does not require that all issuers be treated the same; rather, the Act requires that the rules of an exchange not unfairly discriminate between issuers. The Commission has previously found that offering certain complimentary products and services to issuers that meet specified criteria was consistent with the Act. The Exchange states that it proposes to offer a one-time package of visibility and investor engagement products and services to issuers that have at least 160 million shares outstanding, as opposed to issuers with fewer shares outstanding, as they tend to be larger companies with a larger and more diversified shareholder base and thus have greater demand for visibility and engagement. Additionally, the Exchange states that other exchanges offer complimentary products and services to issuers on a tiered basis based on shares outstanding. For these reasons, the Commission finds that the complimentary services set forth in the proposed rule change, as modified by Amendment No. 1, are equitably allocated among issuers consistent with Section 6(b)(4) of the Act and do not unfairly discriminate between issuers

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BYX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 11.1(a) To Adopt a Start Time Order Instruction
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BYX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 11.1(a) To Adopt a Start Time Order Instruction

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 11.1(a) to adopt a ``Start Time'' order instruction that would permit a User to designate, in thirty-minute increments prior to the commencement of Regular Trading Hours, the time at which an order entered prior to Regular Trading Hours becomes eligible for execution. The proposed rule change is based on EDGX Rule 11.1(a)(2), but the Exchange is proposing to adopt only the Start Time instruction and related provisions. The Exchange intends to implement the proposed rule change on December 7, 2026, in coordination with the implementation of the Start Time instruction on EDGX, so that Members have access to consistent order handling functionality across the Cboe-affiliated equities exchanges. Current Rule Under current Rule 11.1(a), Users may enter orders into the System from 6:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time (``ET''). Orders entered between 6:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m. are not eligible for execution until the start of the Early Trading Session, Pre-Opening Session, or Regular Trading Hours, depending on the Time in Force selected by the User. At the commencement of the Early Trading Session, orders entered between 6:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m. are handled in time sequence, beginning with the order with the oldest time stamp, and are placed on the BYX Book, routed, cancelled, or executed in accordance with the terms of the order. The current rule therefore provides a single, fixed point (the commencement of the Early Trading Session at 7:00 a.m.) at which orders entered prior to the Early Trading Session become eligible for execution, and does not permit a User to designate a later point prior to Regular Trading Hours at which an order becomes eligible. Current Rule 11.1(a) also provides that the Exchange will not accept the following orders prior to 7:00 a.m.: BYX Post Only Orders, ISOs, BYX Market Orders other than those with a Time in Force of Regular Hours Only or Stop Orders, Minimum Quantity Orders that also include a Time in Force of Regular Hours Only, RPI Orders, and all orders with a Time in Force of IOC or FOK. Proposed Start Time Instruction The Exchange proposes to amend the time-sequencing provision so that it is no longer limited to orders entered between 6:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m., and to adopt a flexible Start Time instruction. As proposed, in addition to the Time in Force, a User may also designate a start time for an order (``Start Time''). Start Times may be designated in thirty-minute increments and must be set to a time prior to the commencement of Regular Trading Hours; Start Times may not be designated during Regular Trading Hours. This language is substantively identical to the Start Time language in EDGX Rule 11.1(a)(2), which replaced EDGX's 4:00 a.m. Start and 7:00 a.m. Start designations with the same flexible and uniform framework. Because orders on the Exchange are not eligible for execution prior to the commencement of the Early Trading Session at 7:00 a.m., the earliest Start Time that will have practical effect is 7:00 a.m., and the latest permissible Start Time is 9:00 a.m. The Exchange also proposes to provide that, at the commencement of the Early Trading Session and at each Start Time, orders will be handled in time sequence, beginning with the order with the oldest time stamp, and will be placed on the BYX Book, routed, cancelled, or executed in accordance with the terms of the order. This provision is consistent with the sequencing provision adopted by EDGX, which provides that, at each Start Time, orders will be handled in time sequence beginning with the oldest time stamp. The Exchange proposes to retain the reference to the commencement of the Early Trading Session so that orders that are entered prior to the Early Trading Session without a Start Time designation continue to become eligible for execution, in time sequence, at the commencement of the Early Trading Session, as they do today. For example, a User may enter an order at 6:15 a.m. with a Start Time of 8:00 a.m. That order would be accepted but would not be eligible for execution until 8:00 a.m., at which time it would be handled in time sequence with all other orders designated with an 8:00 a.m. Start Time, beginning with the order with the oldest time stamp, and would be placed on the BYX Book, routed, cancelled, or executed in accordance with its terms. Order Acceptance Restrictions The Exchange proposes to amend the order acceptance restrictions in Rule 11.1(a) so that they apply prior to 7:00 a.m. or, if later, prior to the order's designated Start Time. The Exchange is not proposing any change to the categories of orders subject to these restrictions, which will continue to be: BYX Post Only Orders, ISOs, BYX Market Orders other than those with a Time in Force of Regular Hours Only or Stop Orders, Minimum Quantity Orders that also include a Time in Force of Regular Hours Only, RPI Orders, and all orders with a Time in Force of IOC or FOK. The Exchange is also retaining the existing 7:00 a.m. threshold. Under the proposal, an order in one of these categories designated with a Start Time later than 7:00 a.m. will not be accepted prior to its Start Time. Today, the Exchange does not accept these orders before 7:00 a.m., when orders first become eligible for execution. Tying the restrictions to an order's designated Start Time applies the same approach to the more flexible Start Time framework, so that these orders are not accepted before the point at which the order may execute. EDGX similarly ties its order acceptance restrictions to the period before orders become eligible for execution, which on EDGX is the Order Acceptance Queueing Time. The Exchange is not proposing to change its order entry window, which will continue to begin at 6:00 a.m., or the Time in Force instructions available to Users. Orders entered prior to the Early Trading Session without a Start Time designation will continue to become eligible for execution at the start of the E

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE American LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Modify Binary Return Derivatives Rules
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE American LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Modify Binary Return Derivatives Rules

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to modify Rule 900ByRDs (Applicability; Definitions), Rule 910ByRDs (Determination of the Settlement Price), Rule 915ByRDs (Criteria for Underlying Securities), Rule 916ByRDs (Withdrawal of Approval of Underlying Securities), Rule 958ByRDs (Maximum Bid-Ask Differentials), Rule 980ByRDs (Automatic Exercise of Binary Return Derivatives) and Rule 928.1NYP (Price Reasonability Checks--Orders and Quotes) with respect to trading of ByRDs on the Exchange. More specifically, the Exchange proposes to use the closing price of the security underlying a ByRD options contract as reported by the primary listing market (``Closing Price'') in place of using the ``composite price'' volume weighted average price (``VWAP'') to determine the settlement price of the ByRD options contract on the date of expiration and adopt a new initial and continued listing criteria for ByRDs whose underlying security is an individual stock. The Exchange also proposes to eliminate settlement price rounding practices, instead redefining Finish High ByRDs to return the settlement amount if the underlying security closes at or above the strike price. Overview of ByRDs 3 ByRDs are European-style option contracts on individual stocks, exchange-traded funds (``ETFs'') and Index-Linked Securities that have a fixed return in cash based on a set strike price; satisfy specified listing criteria; and are auto-exercised at expiration pursuant to the Rules of the Options Clearing Corporation (the ``OCC''). ByRDs are binary options and, as such, differ from traditional options traded on U.S. options exchanges by providing a discontinuous or non-linear payout. The payout of a ByRD options contract is an amount contingent upon the occurrence of the option being in- or at-the-money at expiration rather than the degree to which the option is in-the- money. An in-the-money ByRD options contract will pay a fixed sum at expiration regardless of the magnitude of the difference between the option's strike price and the settlement price. A ``Finish High'' ByRD (equivalent to a call option) returns $100 per contract if the settlement price of the underlying security is above the strike price at expiration, and a ``Finish Low'' ByRD (equivalent to a put option) returns $100 per contract if the settlement price of the underlying security is below the strike price at expiration. Currently, Rule 910ByRDs(a) provides that the Exchange will use the ``composite price'' VWAP during regular trading hours for the entire business day of their expiration, or, in the case of an option contract expiring on a day that is not a business day, the entire business day immediately preceding the expiration date. The rule further provides that to calculate the VWAP, the Exchange would use composite prices during regular trading hours as reported by industry price vendors. If the security underlying a ByRDs option contract does not trade or is unavailable during regular trading hours at expiration, the settlement price may be fixed pursuant to the OCC's rules on a basis that the OCC believes is appropriate under the circumstances, including using the last sale price during regular trading hours on the most recent trading day for which a last sale price is available. Exchange rules also currently provide that the settlement price is calculated such that it will always round up $.01 in those instances when the settlement price exactly equals an expiring strike price. For example, if the calculated settlement price is $20.00, and there are expiring ByRDs Finish High and Finish Low contracts with a strike price of $20.00, the settlement price is rounded up to $20.01 so that the Finish High options will pay off. The effect of rounding is to have long $20.00 strike Finish High holders receiving $100.00 and long $20.00 strike Finish Low holders receiving $0. Absent this rounding, a participant may potentially have a position that appears to guarantee a pay-off of $100 at expiration but would instead receive $0. For example, if an investor holds both a $20.00 strike Finish High contract and a $20.00 strike Finish Low contract, the investor will receive $0 if the settlement price was calculated to exactly equal the $20.00 strike price. Although the risk of the settlement price equaling the strike price is small, the Exchange believes that this could cause problems both for hedging and explaining to investors what would happen in the unusual circumstance where the settlement price matched the strike price of an expiring ByRDs option contract exactly. This rounding method ensures that either the Finish High or the Finish Low ByRDs option contracts will always pay off at expiration. The Exchange believes this results in less opportunity for investor confusion and less uncertainty for participants as a whole. Proposed Rule Change The purpose of the proposed rule change is to determine the settlement price of a ByRDs options contract by using the underlying security's Closing Price, in place of using the security's composite price VWAP on the day of expiration. In connection with the proposed rule change, the Exchange proposes the following changes to certain of the rules that permit the listing and trading of ByRDs. First, the Exchange proposes to modify Rule 900ByRDs(b)(1) by amending the definition of ``Binary Return Derivatives,'' maintaining that ByRDs are European-style, but specifying more clearly via a new sentence that ``ByRDs are automatically exercised at expiration pursuant to the Rules of the Options Clearing Corporation, returning the settlement amount, equal to $100, if the underlying security closes (1) at or above the strike price at expiration for Finish High ByRDs or (2) below the strike price at expiration for Finish Low ByRDs.'' The Exchange also proposes to modify Rule 900ByRDs(b)(2) and Rule 900ByRDs(b)(3) to reflect the elimination of settlement price rounding practices, specifying instead that ``Finish High'' ByRDs return $100

Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Article I, Sections 1.05 (Registered Office) and 1.06 (Registered Agent) of the Thirteenth Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of the Exchange (``Operating Agreement'') to reflect the change of the address of the registered office; (b) amend Article II, Section 2.02 (Rules; Supervision of Member Organizations) of the Operating agreement to change cross references; (c) amend Article II, Section 2.03(a) (Board) of the Operating Agreement to reflect the inclusion of Limited Underwriting Members as members, and (c) make certain clarifying, technical and conforming changes to the operating agreement. Proposed Amendments to Article I, Sections 1.05 and 1.06 The Exchange proposes to amend the Operating Agreement to make a technical change updating the address of the registered office of the registered agent in the state of Delaware. The changes are non- substantive technical administrative changes. The Exchange is a limited liability company organized under the laws of the state of Delaware. As such, it has and maintains a registered office and registered agent in Delaware. Article I, Section 1.05 of the Operating Agreement provides that the address of the registered office of the Exchange in the State of Delaware is c/o United Agent Group Inc., 3411 Silverside Road, Tatnall Building No. 104, Wilmington, County of New Castle, State of Delaware, 19810. The Exchange proposes to amend such provision to provide that the address is c/o United Agent Group Inc., 1521 Concord Pike, Suite 201, Wilmington, County of New Castle, State of Delaware 19813. Article I, Section 1.06 of the Operating Agreement provides that the address of the registered agent of the Exchange for service of process on the Exchange in the State of Delaware is Silverside Road, Tatnall Building No. 104, Wilmington, County of New Castle, State of Delaware 19810. The Exchange proposes to amend such provision to provide that the address is 1521 Concord Pike, Suite 201, Wilmington, County of New Castle, State of Delaware 19813. Proposed Amendments to Article II, Section 2.02 The Exchange proposes to amend Section 2.02 to change the cross references. Currently, Section 2.02 refers to members and member organizations ``as defined in Rule 18 and 24 of the Company, respectively'' and to specialists and designated market makers ``as defined in Rule 2 of the Company Rules''. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Investors Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change Pursuant to IEX Rule 15.110(a) and (c) To Amend the Exchange's Fee Schedule To Adopt Transaction Fees and Routing Fees

Self-Regulatory Organizations; Investors Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change Pursuant to IEX Rule 15.110(a) and (c) To Amend the Exchange's Fee Schedule To Adopt Transaction Fees and Routing Fees

1. Purpose In preparation for the October 2, 2026 commencement of trading options on IEX Options, IEX filed a proposed rule change to establish the transaction and routing fees it would charge Options Members. On October 14, 2026, IEX concurrently withdrew the Initial Transaction Fee Filing and replaced it with this proposed rule change, which makes no changes to the fees and credits proposed in the Initial Transaction Fee Filing, but provides additional support and context for certain of the fees and credits. Thus, this filing also (i) defines terms in the Preface and Definitions Sections of the Options Fee Schedule that are used throughout the Options Fee Schedule; (ii) establishes transaction fees and credits applicable to all Options Members trading on IEX Options (``Transaction Fees and Credits''); and (iii) establishes routing fees applicable to all Options Members trading on IEX Options who route orders to away exchanges (``Linkage Routing Fees''). Updates to Preface Section The Options Fee Schedule has a Preface section that currently has one paragraph, which provides information about billing disputes. The Exchange proposes to add a new paragraph directly following the billing disputes paragraph, which describes the rounding of fees that the Exchange would calculate on the basis of transaction volume. Specifically, the Exchange proposes to add a paragraph with the heading ``Rounding,'' which explains that the Exchange would apply the applicable fee rate to the sum of an Option Member's volume for the month and where a fractional cent occurs, the Exchange would round up to the nearest whole cent for purposes of computing the Option Member's invoice. The proposed text reads in full: All volume for the month will be summed and the applicable rate applied. In those cases where a fractional cent occurs, the Exchange will round up to the nearest whole cent for purposes of computing the invoice. The Exchange believes that including this Rounding paragraph in the Preface to the Options Fee Schedule provides clarity about how the Exchange computes fees. The Exchange's proposed language is consistent with similar language included in the fee schedule of one other exchange. Updates to Definitions Section The Exchange includes a Definitions section at the beginning of the Options Fee Schedule for terms that are used throughout the Options Fee Schedule. The purpose of the Definitions section is to streamline the Options Fee Schedule by placing many of the defined terms used in the Options Fee Schedule in one location. For ease of reference and readability, the Exchange proposes adding several definitions to the Definitions section of the Options Fee Schedule, all of which relate to the Transaction Fees and Credits section of the Options Fee Schedule. Many of the defined terms are also defined in the IEX Options Rules, particularly in Rule 17.100. IEX proposes arranging the following definitions in alphabetical order with the previously defined terms in the Options Fee Schedule: An ``Away Market Maker'' for the purposes of this fee schedule shall mean a non-IEX Market Maker. A ``Broker-Dealer'' means an individual or organization registered with the Commission in accordance with Section 15(b)(1) of the Exchange Act or a foreign broker or dealer exempt from such registration pursuant to Rule 15a-6 under the Exchange Act. See Rule 28.100. The ``Exchange System'' or ``System'' means the automated trading system used by IEX Options for the trading of options contracts. See Rule 22.100(a). A ``Firm'' means a Broker-Dealer that is not registered as a Market Maker that is an Options Member of the Exchange. See Rule 28.100. A ``Non-Penny'' option refers to option classes that do not participate in the Penny Interval Program, as described in Rule 22.140. A ``Non-Priority Customer'' means anyone who is not a ``Priority Customer.'' A ``Penny'' option refers to option classes that participate in the Penny Interval Program, as described in Rule 22.140. A ``Priority Customer'' means any person or entity that is not: (A) a broker or dealer in securities; or (B) a Professional. A ``Professional'' means any person or entity that (A) is not a broker or dealer in securities; and (B) places more than 390 orders in listed options per day on average during a calendar month for its own beneficial account(s). The ``Step Up Mechanism'' is a feature within the System that provides automated order handling in designated classes trading for qualifying orders that are not automatically executed by the System. See Rule 22.270. IEX notes that other exchanges similarly set forth certain definitions of terms used in their fee schedules in definitions sections in their respective fee schedules. Transaction Fees and Credits IEX Options generally operates a ``Maker-Taker'' model, whereby it provides credits to Options Members that provide liquidity and charges fees to those that remove liquidity. The proposed credits and fees vary depending on the capacity of the two sides to a transaction, whether the applicable options class participates in the Penny Interval Program (``Penny Classes'') or does not participate in the Penny Interval Program (``Non-Penny Classes''), and whether the transaction adds or removes liquidity from the IEX Options Book. Section I of the Options Fee Schedule, which is titled ``Transaction Fees and Credits,'' is currently ``Reserved.'' IEX proposes to delete the word ``Reserved'' and replace it with language describing the transaction fees and credits in this fee proposal. title: IEX Equities Fee Schedule Updates Operative December 1, 2026
raw_text:
IEX Equities Fee Schedule Updates Operative December 1, 2026
Category: Fee Changes; Alert 2026-039
Overview Effective December 1, 2026, IEX Equities will modify its Displayed Liquidity Adding Rebate Tiers by adding an additional means of qualifying for Tier 8. Under the new qualifying criteria, a Member would qualify for Tier 8 in the current month if, in the immediately preceding month, the Member added at least 35,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity, of which at least 25,000,000 ADV was in non-ETP securities, subject to the effectiveness of SR-IEX-2026-44 . Updated IEX Equities Fee Schedule The updates that will be operative December 1, 2026 are illustrated below. For a complete list of the Fee Code combinations supported by IEX Equities, along with definitions and additional information, please refer to the IEX Equity Fee Schedule. These will be included on execution reports sent by the Exchange to Users in FIX Tag 9730 ("TradeLiquidityIndicator"). ****** 4 Displayed Liquidity Adding Rebate Tiers (Applicable to Executions at or above $1): Tier Required Criteria Fee Tier 1 Member added less than 5,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity FREE Tier 2 Member traded at least 10,000,000 non-displayed ADV and less than 20,000,000 non-displayed ADV ($0.0010) Tier 3 Member: (1) added at least 5,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity and less than 15,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity; or (2) traded at least 20,000,000 non-displayed ADV; or (3) had an NBBO Time of at least 50% in at least 250 ETPs ($0.0014) Tier 4 Member: (1) added at least 15,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity and less than 20,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity; or (2) had an NBBO Time of at least 50% in at least 750 ETPs ($0.0016) Tier 5 Member: (1) added at least 20,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity and less than 25,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity; or (2) traded at least 30,000,000 non-displayed ADV ($0.0018) Tier 6 Member: (1) added at least 25,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity and less than 30,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity; or (2) traded at least 40,000,000 non-displayed ADV ($0.0020) Tier 7 Member added at least 30,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity and less than 40,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity ($0.0021) Tier 8 Member : (1) added at least 40,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity and less than 50,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity ; or (2) added at least 35,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity, at least 25,000,000 ADV of which was in non-ETP securities ($0.0022) Tier 9 Member added at least 50,000,000 ADV of displayed liquidity ($0.0023) ****** Additional Resources Rule Filing: SR-IEX-2026-44 IEX Equities Fee Schedule IEX Exchange FIX Specification IEX Rule Book More Information Please contact IEX Market Operations or Sales with any questions: Market Operations: marketops@iextrading.com Sales: sales@iextrading.com About IEX Exchange Investors’ Exchange LLC (IEX Exchange or IEX) is a national securities exchange designed to provide superior execution quality and set a new standard for trading. IEX operates in both equities (IEX Equities) and options (IEX Options). Since launching in 2016, IEX Equities has grown to be one of the largest exchange operators globally, by notional value traded. In October 2026, IEX launched IEX Options, a new U.S. options exchange that brings its suite of order protection innovations designed to better address the needs of market makers and drive better outcomes for end investors. To learn more visit iex.io .
